Jackman gained his first prize and should develop into a class walker, with perseverance, whilst Larman's continued gradual improvement gained for him third position.

Larman managed to beat Jackman for second place, so reversing their positions of the previous Wednesday. Len Fletcher finished fourth from the scratch mark, having covered the two miles in 14min. 25sec. and showed excellent form.
Jackman, second, also again showed improved form, and in A. Maynard, the winner of the One Mile Novice Walk, we have another young walker likely to strengthen our teams in due course.
Heather and Jackman, also of the "younger" brigade, finished second and third; and fourth came Len Fletcher from the scratch mark, in the fastest time he has ever recorded on the Battersea track.

Joe Coleman started off splendidly and although he slackened off a little in the second half of the race, he did well to take the handicap prize. Our team, consisting of Coleman, Jackman, Speechley and C.

Ted Jackman and Jim Latter had a determined struggle for second place, but Latter's earlier efforts in catching the leaders had sapped his strength, and Jackman was able to draw away in the last hundred yards.
Jackman, for us, walked very impressively to finish fourth and shows improvement at every outing; our other man being Storey, who punished himself to finish seventh.
We were successful on this occasion, Jackman, Brown and Harley forming our trio. Among those who have been successful in Walk handicaps on the track recently are J.
Elson (9), Harley (10), Martin (11), Bidgood (12), J. Field (18), Jackman (21).
Our track walkers have been showing up well in the Open handicap prize lists lately and names which have caught the eye are Brown, Storey, Harley, Rutland, Jackman, C.
